Bug_Title: PERM: Custom class loader does not call its superclass’s getPermissions() (PERM_SUPER_NOT_CALLED_IN_GETPERMISSIONS)
Bug_Details:
SEI CERT rule SEC07-J requires that custom class loaders must always call their superclass's getPermissions()
method in their own getPermissions() method to initialize the object they return at the end. Omitting it means
that a class defined using this custom class loader has permissions that are completely independent of those
specified in the systemwide policy file. In effect, the class's permissions override them.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the getPermissions() method of the CustomClassLoader class. The superclass's getPermissions() method is not called, which results in the permissions object not being initialized with the permissions specified in the systemwide policy file. This means that a class defined using this custom class loader has permissions that are completely independent of those specified in the systemwide policy file.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the custom class loader does not call its superclass’s getPermissions() method, causing the loaded class to have permissions that are completely independent of those specified in the systemwide policy file. This is verified in the test case by setting a custom policy with a test permission and checking if the loaded class's permissions include this test permission, which they should not.
